page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-intensive workloads requiring a very high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance is powered by an x86_64 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache, 128.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, and 118 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Network throughput starts with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no GPU hardware is attached.

Benchmark metrics reflect the instance's deliberate architectural balance toward extreme memory density rather than raw parallel compute. Single-core performance sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1647.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1890.78. Conversely, multi-core throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU footprint, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 5862.72 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 19.72 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth register at 28.82 GB/sec and 25.24 GB/sec respectively, while PassMark memory testing ranks in the average range at 2227.36.

The cost-efficiency profile of the x2iedn.xlarge is defined by its 32 GB per core memory allocation. Rather than scaling up to larger compute instances solely to satisfy large working sets, organizations can minimize compute costs while gaining access to 128 GB of RAM and fast local temporary storage. This hardware balance makes the instance suitable for in-memory caches, memory-bound databases, electronic design automation, and operational analytics workloads that demand large memory footprints without intense multi-threaded processor capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System using x86_64 architecture, it delivers an extraordinary 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, resulting in a 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 118 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-thread performance, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1647.0, alongside lower aggregate multi-threaded scores constrained by its 4 vCPUs. The hardware configuration offers cost efficiency for memory-dominated workloads by eliminating the requirement to provision unneeded compute capacity to satisfy high memory demands, making it well matched for in-memory databases, key-value stores, and caching layers.
